note: The rig rule, written down once. lib/main.dart's rigFamilyFromMarkers
and atlas_mcp.py's rig_family_from_markers are separate implementations
of it in two languages -- the arrangement that always drifts, and this
one had: graded against which clip rig actually names each character's
bones, over 800 rigged characters, the Python rule was right 786 times
and the Dart rule 480. Neither side owns the rule now. Both suites read
this file, and a case added here fails on whichever side has not caught
`markers` is what the importer's --probe reports for a file, which is
the subset of kRigMarkerBones (mesh_importer.cpp) the file carries, and
`bones` is the skeleton's bone count from the same probe.

families.why: Synty's own rig, capitalised. 39 of 300 probed files.
A Sidekick character: the mannequin plus attachment and IK bones.
A Sidekick clip. 81 of 300. No hips marker, but the IK bones are there.
One attachment bone is enough; nothing else carries them.
An IK bone alone is also enough.
The mannequin with only its upper markers probed. 40 of 300.
Exactly two Polygon markers is the floor for polygon.
Exactly two mannequin markers is the floor for unreal.
Kenney's 58-bone Blender rig shares exactly one name with Polygon. One marker must not name a family -- 13 clips were stored as polygon on this.
One Polygon marker, the other spelling. Still not a family.
One marker from each family is not evidence for either.
The Dogs pack: a real 82-bone rig with no marker bone at all. Its mesh and its 88 clips are on it, and calling this 'none' is what stopped them pairing.
A prop. No bones, so no rig, whatever else is true of it.
Bone count decides first: marker names with no skeleton is a file the probe read as geometry only.
Sidekick is tested before the mannequin it extends, or every Sidekick file reads as unreal.
Both capitalisations present and both over the threshold: Polygon is tested first, so it wins. Not seen in the library; pinned so the two languages cannot disagree about it.

compatibleNote: Whether a clip on `clip` can drive a character on `character`.
`sameContainer` says whether the two files came out of the same pack,
which only matters for a rig neither side can name.

compatible.why: The Sidekick rig is the Unreal mannequin with bones added, so a Sidekick clip names every bone an Unreal character has. The library holds no unreal clips at all, so equality alone matched 0 of 796 for 348 characters.
Polygon shares not one bone name with either mannequin rig.
Two rigs nobody has named are the same rig only if they shipped together. The Dogs pack's mesh and clips are in one zip.
Two unnamed rigs from different packs are two different rigs until something reads their bones.
An unnamed rig is not a mannequin, even in the same pack.
A prop has no bones for a clip to move.
And a clip with no skeleton moves nothing.
